misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program PanjangKataTerpanjang
kamus
  n, i, panjangMax, panjangSekarang : integer
  kata : string
algoritma
  input(n)
  panjangMax <- 0
  i <- 1
  if i <= n then
    input(kata)
    panjangSekarang <- panjang(kata)
    if panjangSekarang > panjangMax then
      panjangMax <- panjangSekarang
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(panjangMax)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with an if-statement, using an index-based approach. They increment the index (idx) within the if-statement body and check if idx < len(list1). The student genuinely believes this if-statement will continue executing repeatedly as long as idx < len(list1), similar to how a while loop would behave. From their perspective, this should iterate through all elements in the list and find the maximum length. In reality, the if-statement only executes once, so the code will only check at most the second element (index 1) and then return, missing all other elements in the list.
